item.text: {"search_note":"I found indirect evidence that Khamenei allowed a somewhat more technocratic cabinet to pass, but I did not find a 2024 source showing Khamenei personally appointing a dedicated economic team or directly choosing economic professionals over loyalists. The evidence is mostly about his approval/veto environment and the composition of Pezeshkian’s cabinet, so the best-supported reading is “some constrained technocracy, but not a clear Khamenei-led meritocratic appointment pattern.”","evidence":[{"title":"Pezeshkian Cabinet: Profiles","publisher":"The Iran Primer","date":"2024-08-22","url":"https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/aug/22/pezeshkian-cabinet-profiles","summary":"Iran’s new cabinet included reformists, hardliners, technocrats, and academics with no political affiliations. The article also says Pezeshkian had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submitting the list.
